bc_the_zen_garden_main_area.blurb: Set in forest beside Shannon Falls near Squamish, this is the larger upper section of the Zen Garden. It is a gear-climbing venue: sixteen trad lines and a single bolted one, with most grades sitting in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, a few easier 5.7 to 5.9 options and one 5.12. Crack climbing is the main attraction, from thin fingers up to ringlock splitters. The wall faces west, so it is pleasant before the afternoon sun arrives, and most lines dry quickly after rain, though seepage can linger in wet spells. Reaching the base takes a short, steep effort, and the cliff also has boulder problems along its foot.

bc_downtown_eastside.blurb: A compact sport crag in the Comox Lake climbing zone on Vancouver Island, close to the road and a short walk up switchbacks from the lakeside parking. All seventeen routes are bolted and the grade range is wide, from easy 5.6 up to 5.12, with the biggest cluster at 5.11 and a handful of friendlier 5.6 to 5.10 lines. It is regarded as a good place for newer leaders to get started, while stronger climbers have plenty to work on. A second tier of rock sits a short way up and right of the first wall, and more crags lie beyond.

bc_conroy_s_castle.blurb: Conroy's Castle is a sixteen-route sport crag in Chek, the Cheakamus Canyon climbing zone north of Squamish on Highway 99. It sits beside the forest road just below the top parking area, so walking time is minimal. What sets it apart in Chek is the lower-angle rock, which gives a rare supply of approachable climbing: most routes fall between 5.8 and 5.10, with a few easier ones and some two-pitch outings. Higher grades are absent, making this a sensible choice for those building up mileage or warming up before harder walls nearby. Views stretch toward the Tantalus Range.

bc_echo_beach.blurb: Echo Beach is a hard-leaning sport crag perched high above the Main Event and Big Show walls in Chek, the Cheakamus Canyon zone near Squamish. All sixteen routes fall in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with 5.12 the more common. The left side is gently overhanging and pumpy on mostly positive holds, while the right side eases back into steeper slab with bulges where friction matters. Several lines dry fast after rain, which helps on damp days. The crag opened relatively recently, has good mountain views, and suits climbers comfortable on sustained, technical sport pitches rather than beginners.
